summary: Argus is a web-based smart agriculture platform that helps farmers monitor their fields using maps and NASA Earth observation resources. Users can create an account, draw field boundaries on an interactive map, and store them as GeoJSON with PostGIS-based area calculations. The application displays NASA GIBS satellite imagery, searches NASA’s HLS and HLS-VI catalogs for field-related observation metadata, and retrieves daily weather data from NASA POWER. Its backend also includes an AppEEARS workflow for requesting HLS-VI rasters with matching quality data; real NDVI rasters can support transparent risk screening rather than unverified diagnoses. Farmers can securely upload field photos, but disease diagnosis remains unavailable until a trained and validated model is provided. Argus is important because it brings satellite, weather, and field information into one practical tool while clearly distinguishing available data from pending or unavailable analysis.
details:
Argus is a responsive web application for field management and agricultural monitoring. Farmers can create accounts, map multiple fields, save field boundaries as GeoJSON, and view field areas calculated using PostGIS. The map combines Leaflet, OpenStreetMap, and NASA GIBS imagery. The backend makes live requests to NASA CMR for HLS and HLS-VI catalog metadata and to NASA POWER for daily weather data. It also contains an AppEEARS workflow for requesting HLS-VI raster products with corresponding HLS Fmask quality data. When real, quality-screened NDVI rasters are available, the system can create risk-screening zones; these are not crop diagnoses or expert-calibrated predictions.

Farmers can upload JPEG, PNG, or WebP field photos with file validation. A MobileNetV3-Small training and inference pipeline is included, but no trained, validated disease-model weights or disease-image dataset are supplied, so the app does not claim to diagnose plant diseases. The platform was built with Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL/PostGIS, Leaflet, Rasterio, Pillow, and a Redis/Celery processing architecture. The frontend is deployed at https://argusearth.photo.

SI-use disclosure: GitHub Copilot, a generative AI tool, assisted with code development, debugging, and written descriptions. Generated code and text were reviewed and tested. No AI-generated images, videos, or audio are used, and no NASA logos or branding were generated or modified.
